--- title: Decalendar description: > Introducing Decalendar, a solar calendar which measures time in years and days without the need for months or weeks. image: /asset/cal16.svg url: https://maptv.github.io/dec/date decdate: 2026+242 path: /dec/date slug: date aliases: - /date - /dd engine: knitr crossref: fig-prefix: Diagram fig-title: Diagram nocite: | @c3s2018era5hourly, @hersbach2020era5 --- :::{.datenav #topdatenav} ::: # Decalendar {#decalendar .hiddenheading} My website serves as a demonstration of both the [Quarto](https://quarto.org) publishing📤system and the [Dec](/dec) measurement📐system. I use several clever hacks to get Quarto to display all of the dates on my website in the Dec year+day format. Knowing the basics of the Dec calendar🗓️(Decalendar) will help you to understand the [filter](https://quarto.org/docs/extensions/filters.html) and [include](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-basics.html#includes) articles in the [Quarto section](/quarto) of my site. Among its many features, Quarto offers support for the [Observable](https://observablehq.com/) data visualization system. Observable is my top choice for interactive graphics. You can interact with the two Observable [calendar plots](https://observablehq.com/@observablehq/plot-calendar) below⬇️using the adjacent Observable [inputs](https://observablehq.com/documentation/inputs/overview). The [scrubber](https://observablehq.com/@mbostock/scrubber)🧽input is a great place to start because it cycles🔄through every value of the [range](https://observablehq.com/@observablehq/input-range)🎚️inputs beneath it. # Day of year (doy) {#sec-doy} To activate the scrubber input, press the "Play"▶️button adjacent to the range inputs. Upon activation, the box around the selected day in each plot will move back and forth between the first "day of year" ([doy](#doy){#dayofyear .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of year"}), [d](#d){#day .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[0]{.color0}, and the last [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of year"}, which is either [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[364]{.color364by365} or [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[365]{.color365by366}. To insert or remove [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[365]{.color365by366}, use the "Year length" [radio](https://observablehq.github.io/framework/inputs/radio#:~:text=allows%20the%20user%20to%20choose%20one%20of%20a%20given%20set%20of%20values)📻input to set the number of days in the year. The insertion of [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[365]{.color365by366} shifts 306 dates, [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}\${march1doyColor} to [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}\${december31doyColor}, in the [Gregorian calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregorian_calendar#:~:text=the%20calendar%20used%20in%20most%20parts%20of%20the%20world) by 1 day, but does not change the order of any Dec dates, because [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[365]{.color365by366} is the last day of any Dec leap year and is always followed by [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[0]{.color0} of the subsequent Dec year ([y](#y){#year .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="year"}+1). The "Year length" radio input also changes the value of the negative "Day of year" range input by 1 day. Similarly, the "[Coordinated Universal Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time#:~:text=the%20primary%20time%20standard%20globally%20used%20to%20regulate%20clocks%20and%20time) ([UTC](#utc){#coordinateduniversaltime .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Coordinated Universal Time"}) [offset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC_offset#:~:text=the%20difference%20in%20hours%20and%20minutes%20between%20Coordinated%20Universal%20Time%20(UTC)%20and%20the%20standard%20time%20at%20a%20particular%20place)" radio input shifts the Gregorian calendar date selected by the "Month" and "Day of month" range inputs by 1 day. If the "[Color scheme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Color_scheme#:~:text=a%20combination%20of%202%20or%20more%20colors%20used%20in%20aesthetic%20or%20practical%20design)" radio input is set to "Month" instead of "Day", the "[UTC](#utc){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Coordinated Universal Time"} offset" radio input will also rotate the Dec colors🎨(Decolors) inside the [cells](https://observablehq.com/plot/marks/cell) of both calendar plots by 1 day. From the perspective of Dec, month Decolors are only useful if we want to compare the Dec and Gregorian calendars. In contrast, day Decolors can help us organize days into groups of 100 called [hectodays]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hundreds of days"} ([h](#h){#hectoday .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of one hundred days"}) and groups of 10 named [xún](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_calendar#:~:text=into%20nine%2D%20or-,ten%2Dday%20weeks,-known%20as%20x%C3%BAn) ([x](#x){#xun .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of ten days"}). Dec defines [meteorological seasons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season#Meteorological:~:text=reckoned%20by%20temperature) in terms of [h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of one hundred days"} and uses [x](#x){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of ten days"} in place of Gregorian calendar months and weeks. The "Plot layout" radio input pivots the calendar plots by a quarter [turn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn_%28angle%29#:~:text=the%20Greek%20letter,to%20one%20turn), interchanging the horizontal (↔) and vertical (↕) axes. To make [lim](#lim){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="liminal interconnecting margin"} appear more like weekends we can start from [Dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} [1]{.color1} instead of [Dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} [0]{.color0} as in @fig-one below, which displays its [lim](#lim){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="liminal interconnecting margin"} as a two-by-two square on the right like [Lim](#lim){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="liminal interconnecting margin"} [73]{.color364by366} and [1]{.color004} in @fig-zeroleap above. ::: {.centered} ### Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} ([Dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} [1]{.color1} to [0]{.color0}) {.diagtitle} ::: ::: {#fig-one .doxdiagram} ```{mermaid} %%| mermaid-format: svg %%{init: {'theme': 'default', 'themeVariables': { 'fontSize': '29px'}}}%% flowchart LR B~~~M[ ]:::empty----N[ ]:::empty W---M N---O[ ]:::empty Q[ ]:::empty---L W[ ]:::empty-->A[1]-->B[2]-->C[3]-->D[4]-->E[5]---L[ ]:::empty Y[ ]:::empty-->F[6]-->G[7]-->H[8]-->I[9]-->J[0]---O[ ]:::empty B~~~P[ ]:::empty---Q Y---P subgraph workdays[work] A B C F G H end subgraph restdays[ ] D E I J workdays end classDef empty width:0px; ``` ::: The order of [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} in @fig-one is different from all of the previous diagrams, but all of the diagrams above show Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} because the categorization of [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} as work or rest days remains unchanged. If we left [rotate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circular_shift#:~:text=moving%20the%20final%20entry%20to%20the%20first%20position%2C%20while%20shifting%20all%20other%20entries%20to%20the%20next%20position%2C%20or%20by%20performing%20the%20inverse%20operation) (↺) the [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} categories of Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} by 1 day, we get the Schedule [X]{.color28by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal X is decimal 28 or binary 11100"} Dec schedule: [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} ↺ 1 = [X]{.color28by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal X is decimal 28 or binary 11100"}. Schedule [X]{.color28by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal X is decimal 28 or binary 11100"} groups rest days at the end of each [p](#p){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="pentaday"}. ::: {.centered} ### Schedule [X]{.color28by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal X is decimal 28 or binary 11100"} ([Dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} [0]{.color0} to [9]{.color9}) {.diagtitle} ::: ::: {#fig-xpos .doxdiagram} ```{mermaid} %%| mermaid-format: svg %%{init: {'theme': 'default', 'themeVariables': { 'fontSize': '29px'}}}%% flowchart LR B~~~M[ ]:::empty----N[ ]:::empty W---M N---O[ ]:::empty Q[ ]:::empty---L W[ ]:::empty-->A[0]-->B[1]-->C[2]-->D[3]-->E[4]---L[ ]:::empty Y[ ]:::empty-->F[5]-->G[6]-->H[7]-->I[8]-->J[9]---O[ ]:::empty B~~~P[ ]:::empty---Q Y---P subgraph workdays[work] A B C F G H end subgraph restdays[ ] D E I J workdays end classDef empty width:0px; ``` ::: If we adhere to Schedule [X]{.color28by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal X is decimal 28 or binary 11100"}, there will be 4 consecutive work days during any transition from a leap year. To limit the number of consecutive work days to 3, we could right rotate (↻) Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} and obtain Schedule [F]{.color07by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal F is decimal 7 or binary 00111"}: [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} ↻ 1 = [F]{.color07by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal F is decimal 7 or binary 00111"}. Unlike Schedule [X]{.color28by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal X is decimal 28 or binary 11100"}, Schedules [F]{.color07by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal F is decimal 7 or binary 00111"} and [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} handle yearly transitions gracefully and always provision exactly 219 work days per year. ::: {.centered} ### Schedule [F]{.color07by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal F is decimal 7 or binary 00111"} ([Dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} [0]{.color0} to [9]{.color9}) {.diagtitle} ::: ::: {#fig-fpos .doxdiagram} ```{mermaid} %%| mermaid-format: svg %%{init: {'theme': 'default', 'themeVariables': { 'fontSize': '29px'}}}%% flowchart LR M[ ]:::empty----N[ ]:::empty W---M N---O[ ]:::empty Q[ ]:::empty---L W[ ]:::empty-->A[0]-->B[1]-->C[2]-->D[3]-->E[4]---L[ ]:::empty Y[ ]:::empty-->F[5]-->G[6]-->H[7]-->I[8]-->J[9]---O[ ]:::empty P[ ]:::empty---Q Y---P subgraph workdays[work] C D E H I J end subgraph restdays[ ] A B F G workdays end classDef empty width:0px; ``` ::: There are 32 Dec schedules which can be expressed as a five-bit ([5b]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="five-bit"}) [binary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binary_number#:~:text=only%20two%20symbols%20for%20the%20natural%20numbers%3A%20typically%200%20%28zero%29%20and%201%20%28one%29) ([[base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radix#:~:text=the%20number%20of%20unique%20digits)2]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="binary"}) sequence. Of these 32 binary sequences, 8 are [palindromes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palindrome#:~:text=reads%20the%20same%20backwards%20as%20forwards). If a Dec schedule can be represented by a [5b]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="five-bit"} palindrome such as [01110]{.color14by32}, we can identify its work and rest days by the last digit of an [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer days of year"} with an [acute accent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acute_accent#:~:text=a%20diacritic%20used%20in%20many%20modern%20written%20languages%20with%20alphabets%20based%20on%20the%20Latin%2C%20Cyrillic%2C%20and%20Greek%20scripts) ([ni[d]{.acute}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}) in common years or a double acute accent ([ni[d]{.doubleacute}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}) in leap years. We can sum an [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} with 1 to get an [ni[d]{.acute}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}, [ni[d]{.acute}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} = [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} + 1, or with 2 to get an [ni[d]{.doubleacute}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}: [ni[d]{.doubleacute}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} = [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} + 2. @tbl-vincommon below displays the [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer days of year"}, [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}, [ni[d]{.acute}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}, and "mixed integer [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of year"}" ([mid](#mid){#mixedintegerdoy .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"}) of the first and last 11 days of a common year. We can use the last digit of any [mid](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"} that is derived from an [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} to discern between the work and rest days of any of the 32 Dec [5b]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="five-bit"} schedules in common years. The horizontal line above all but the last digit of each [[mi]{.overline}d](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"} in @tbl-vincommon is called a [vinculum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinculum_(symbol)#:~:text=a%20horizontal%20line%20used%20in%20mathematical%20notation%20for%20various%20purposes). In Dec, a vinculum negates any digit beneath it. A negated zero is equal to zero: [-0]{.color0} = [[0]{.overline}]{.color0} = [0]{.color0}. Day [-1]{.color364by365}, [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[[1]{.overline}]{.color364by365}, and [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[[1]{.overline}9]{.color364by365} all denote the last day of the Dec year: [-1]{.color364by365} = [[1]{.overline}]{.color364by365} = [[1]{.overline}9]{.color364by365} = -10 + 9. The current Dec countdown date can be written as \${nextYearColor()}−\${TminusPaddedColor()}, \${nextYearColor()}+[\${TminusPaddedColor()}]{.overline}, [guanine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guanine#:~:text=one%20of%20the%20four%20main%20nucleotide%20bases), the pattern is [0]{.color0} to [[4]{.acute}]{.color5}, [1]{.color1} to [[3]{.acute}]{.color4}, [2]{.color2} to [[2]{.acute}]{.color3}, [3]{.color3} to [[1]{.acute}]{.color2}, [4]{.color4} to [[0]{.acute}]{.color1}, and so on. The final digits of [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer days of year"} and [ni[d]{.doubleacute}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer days of year"} follow the same pattern in leap years: [0]{.color0} to [[4]{.doubleacute}]{.color6}, [1]{.color1} to [[3]{.doubleacute}]{.color5}, [2]{.color2} to [[2]{.doubleacute}]{.color4}, [3]{.color3} to [[1]{.doubleacute}]{.color3}, [4]{.color4} to [[0]{.doubleacute}]{.color2}, and so on. The last digits of [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer days of year"} and [[mi]{.overline}d](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer days of year"} are misaligned by 4 [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days"} in leap years and by 5 [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days"} in common years. Dec maintains the appearance of a misalignment of 5 [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days"} in leap years by adding 1 to each [[mi]{.overline}d](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer days of year"} and placing a [grave accent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grave_accent#:~:text=a%20diacritical%20mark%20used%20to%20varying%20degrees%20in%20French%2C%20Dutch%2C%20Portuguese%2C%20Italian%2C%20Catalan%20and%20many%20other%20Western%20European%20languages) over its final digit: [[mi]{.overline}d](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer days of year"} + 1 = [[mi]{.overline}[d]{.grave}](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer days of year"}. In general, actual [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of year"} such as [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} or [[mi]{.overline}d](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer days of year"} are 1 or 2 less than their apparent [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of year"} counterparts: [ni[d]{.acute}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}, [ni[d]{.doubleacute}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}, or [[mi]{.overline}[d]{.grave}](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"}. ::: {.centered} ### Leap year examples The absolute value of an [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} is increased by an acute accent ([ni[d]{.acute}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}) and decreased by a grave accent ([ni[d]{.grave}](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}), but the opposite is true for [[mi]{.overline}d](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer days of year"}. The main purpose of Dec accents is to change the appearance of the final digit of an [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} or [[mi]{.overline}d](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer days of year"} so that it can be used just like the last digit of a [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} for work-or-rest-day classification. The Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} rule for categorization of work and rest days can be summarized as [\[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iverson_bracket#:~:text=is%20defined%20to%20take%20the%20value%201%20for%20the%20values%20of%20the%20variables%20for%20which%20the%20statement%20is%20true%2C%20and%20takes%20the%20value%200%20otherwise){.nounder}[dop](#dop){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of pentaday"} ∈ {[1]{.color2},[2]{.color4},[3]{.color6}}[\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iverson_bracket#:~:text=is%20defined%20to%20take%20the%20value%201%20for%20the%20values%20of%20the%20variables%20for%20which%20the%20statement%20is%20true%2C%20and%20takes%20the%20value%200%20otherwise){.nounder}, where ∈ means "is an element of" and {[1]{.color2},[2]{.color4},[3]{.color6}} is Set [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"}, a [set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_(mathematics)#:~:text=a%20set%20is-,a%20collection%20of%20different%20things,-%5B1%5D) which contains all of the [dop]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of pentaday"} that are Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} work days. The Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} rule applies to the last digit of the [[mi]{.overline}d]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"} or [ni[d]{.acute}]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"} in common years, of the [[mi]{.overline}[d]{.grave}]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"} or [ni[d]{.doubleacute}]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"} in leap years, or of the [pid]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer days of year"} in all years. ## Base32 {#b32 .hiddenheading} Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} can be expressed in Dec [duotrigesimal](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/duotrigesimal#:~:text=Based%20upon%20the%20number%20thirty%2Dtwo) ([base32]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal"}) as [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"}, in [decimal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decimal#:~:text=a%20numeral%20system%20that%20uses%20ten%20as%20its%20radix%20%28base%29) ([base10]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="decimal"}) as [14]{.color14by32}, or in [base2]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="binary"} as [01110]{.color14by32}, where 0 is a rest day and 1 is a work day. In contrast to weekly schedules, Dec schedules like [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="L in base32 is 14 in base10 and 01110 in base2"} and [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="L in base32 is 14 in base10 and 01110 in base2"}[M]{.color15by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="M in base32 is 15 in base10 and 01111 in base2"} produce a consistent🎯number of work days every year. While Days [364]{.color364by365}, [365]{.color365by366}, and [0]{.color0} can be work or rest days in the Gregorian calendar, these days are always rest days if we comply with Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="L in base32 is 14 in base10 and 01110 in base2"} or [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="L in base32 is 14 in base10 and 01110 in base2"}[M]{.color15by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="M in base32 is 15 in base10 and 01111 in base2"}. Therefore, Schedules [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="L in base32 is 14 in base10 and 01110 in base2"} and [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="L in base32 is 14 in base10 and 01110 in base2"}[M]{.color15by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="M in base32 is 15 in base10 and 01111 in base2"} do not require any holidays to smooth the transition between years. There are 11 United States (US) [Federal holidays](https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/). US Federal holidays that fall on a Gregorian calendar rest day, [Dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} [0]{.color0 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Sunday"} or [Dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} [6]{.color6by7 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Saturday"}, are observed on the nearest Gregorian calendar work day: [Dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} [1]{.color1by7 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Monday"} or [Dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} [5]{.color5by7 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Friday"}. Rather than apply this rule to Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"} and move holidays from [Dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} [0]{.color0} to [1]{.color1}, [4]{.color4} to [3]{.color3}, [5]{.color5} to [6]{.color6}, or [9]{.color9} to [8]{.color8}, we can switch between Dec schedules as needed. Over the course of a Dec cycle, which consists of 400 years, 20871 weeks, or 146097 [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days"}, a five-day workweek provides an average of 260.8875 work days per year. If we round 260.8875 to 261 and then subtract the 11 US Federal holidays, we get an annual total of 250 work days, which is 1 [p](#p){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="pentaday"} less than the total work days provided annually by Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"}[M]{.color15by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal M is decimal 15 or binary 01111"}. The yearly work day total of Schedule [L]{.color14by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal L is decimal 14 or binary 01110"}[M]{.color15by32 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="duotrigesimal M is decimal 15 or binary 01111"} would be 249 if Days [19]{.color019}, [111]{.color111by365}, [149]{.color149by365}, [206]{.color206by365}, [296]{.color296by365}, and [316]{.color316by365} were reclassified as rest days. The last US Federal holiday of the Gregorian calendar year is [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas#:~:text=annual%20festival%20commemorating%20the%20birth%20of%20Jesus%20Christ)🎄. Although it occurs on [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[299]{.color299by365}, which is the last day of [Hectoday]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hundreds of days"} [2]{.color200by365} ([h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of one hundred days"}[2]{.color200by365}), Christmas is likely to be celebrated on [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[300]{.color300by365}, the first day of [Hectoday]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hundreds of days"} [3]{.color300by365} ([h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of one hundred days"}[3]{.color300by365}), by people who do not use Dec and live in a [UTC](#utc){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Coordinated Universal Time"} time zone with a negative offset. The Dec analog of the [holiday season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_and_holiday_season#:~:text=an%20annual%20period%20generally%20spanning%20from%20November%20or%20December%20to%20early%20January%20incorporating%20Christmas%20Day%20and%20New%20Year%27s%20Day) is [Hectoday]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hundreds of days"} [-1]{.color265by365} ([h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of one hundred days"}[[1]{.overline}]{.color265by365}). # Day of hectoday (doh) {#sec-doh} [Astronomical seasons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Season#Astronomical) vary in duration. The length of a meteorological season is 2 months in the [Hindu calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_calendar#Solar_months_and_seasons:~:text=approximate%20correspondence%20to-,Hindu%20seasons,-%28%E1%B9%9Atu%29%20and), 3 months in the Gregorian calendar, 3 months, 9 [x](#x){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of ten days"}, or 90 [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days"} in the [French Revolutionary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Republican_calendar#Design:~:text=There%20were%20twelve%20months%2C%20each%20divided%20into%20three%2010%2Dday%20weeks%20called%20d%C3%A9cades) calendar, 4 months, 12 [x](#x){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of ten days"}, or 120 [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days"} in the [Egyptian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_calendar#:~:text=Each%20season%20was%20divided%20into%20four%20months%20of%2030%20days.%20These%20twelve%20months%20were%20initially%20numbered%20within%20each%20season%20but%20came%20to%20also%20be%20known%20by%20the%20names%20of%20their%20principal%20festivals.%20Each%20month%20was%20divided%20into%20three%2010%2Dday%20periods%20known%20as%20decans%20or%20decades) calendar, 13 weeks or 91 [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days"} in the [World Season Calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Asimov#Calendar:~:text=divides%20the%20year%20into%20four%20seasons%20%28named%20A%E2%80%93D%29%20of%2013%20weeks%20%2891%20days%29%20each), and 1 [h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="group of one hundred days"}, 10 [x](#x){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of ten days"}, 20 [p](#p){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="pentadays"}, or 100 [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days"} in Decalendar. As opposed to seasons in other calendars, the 4 Dec seasons are chosen from 2 overlapping sets of 4 consecutive [h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of one hundred days"}, called "positive integer hectodays" ([pih](#pih){#positiveintegerhectoday .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer hectodays"}) and "negative integer hectodays" ([nih](#nih){#negativeintegerhectoday .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectodays"}), to match [daily global mean temperature](https://pulse.climate.copernicus.eu) patterns. The [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of year"} in a year+day Dec date is [zero padded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padding_(cryptography)#Zero_padding:~:text=be%20padded%20are-,padded%20with%20zero,-.%20The%20zero%20padding) to three digits. If the three-digit [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of year"} is a [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"}: \${decDotyPadColor()}, its first digit is a [pih](#pih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer hectoday"}: \${decPih}, its last two digits are a [doh](#doh){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of hectoday"}: \${decDohPidColor()}, its first two digits are a [pix](#pix){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer xún"}: \${decDekColor}, and its final digit is a [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"}: \${decDotdColor}. Whereas a [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} gives us information on the current [pix](#pix){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer xún"} and [pih](#pih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer hectoday"}, an [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} tells us about the [nix](#nix){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer xún"} and [nih](#nih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectoday"} that either are coming up next or began today. The three-digit [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} in a year+day Dec date, [\${TminusColor()}]{.overline}, presents an [nih](#nih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectoday"} with its first digit: [\${decNihPlus1Color()}]{.overline}, the days until that [nih](#nih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectoday"} with its last two digits: [\${decDohNidPadColor()}]{.overline}, an [nix](#nix){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer xún"} with its first two digits: [\${decNixPlus1Color()}]{.overline}, and the days until that [nix](#nix){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer xún"} with its final digit: [\${decDoxNidColor}]{.overline}. An [nih](#nih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectoday"} [mid](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"}, [\${decNihAbsColor()}]{.overline}\${decDohNidMidPadColor()}, shows the current [nih](#nih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectoday"} with its first digit: [\${decNihAbsColor()}]{.overline}, a [doh](#doh){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of hectoday"} with its final two digits: \${decDohNidMidPadColor()}, an [nih](#nih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectoday"} "mixed integer xún" ([mix](#mix){#mixedintegerxun .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer xún"}) with its first two digits: [\${decNihAbsColor()}]{.overline}\${decDohNidMidFirstColor()}, and a [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} with its last digit: \${decDoxNidMidColor()}. During [h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="group of one hundred days"}[[1]{.overline}]{.color265by365}, Dec recommends using [nih](#nih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectoday"} [mid](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"} in lieu of [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} for personal timekeeping because [nih](#nih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectodays"} [mid](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"} take into account the [eoy](#eoy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="end of year"} and thus avoid any uncertainty regarding when the year will end. Conversion of an [nih](#nih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectoday"} [mix](#mix){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer xún"} to an [nix](#nix){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer xún"} only requires simple arithmetic: [\${decNihAbsColor()}]{.overline}\${decDohNidMidFirstColor()} = -\${decNihAbsColor()}[0]{.color0} + \${decDohNidMidFirstColor()} = [\${decNixAbsColor()}]{.overline}. If we then append a [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"}, we get an [nix](#nix){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer xún"} [mid](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"} like those in @tbl-vincommon: [\${decNixAbsColor()}]{.overline}\${decDoxNidMidColor()}. During a leap year, we should put a grave accent above the [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} in [nih](#nih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectoday"} and [nix](#nix){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer xún"} [mid](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer days of year"} as in @tbl-vinculeap to facilitate classification of work and rest days according to Dec schedules: [\${decNihGraveColor}]{.overline}\${decDohGraveFirstColor}[\${decDoxGraveColor()}]{.grave} = [\${decNixGraveColor}]{.overline}[\${decDoxGraveColor()}]{.grave} = [\${decNihAbsColor()}]{.overline}\${decDohNidMidPadColor()} = [\${decNixAbsColor()}]{.overline}\${decDoxNidMidColor()}. We can see that [h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="group of one hundred days"}\${decPihColor} is \${decDohPidColor()}% done from the current [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"}: \${decDotyColor()}, [h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="group of one hundred days"}\${decPihPlus1Color()} will begin after the remaining \${decDohPidMidColor()}% of [h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="group of one hundred days"}\${decPih} expires from the current [pih](#pih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer hectoday"} [mid](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"}: \${decPihPlus1Color()}[\${decDohPidMidPadColor}]{.overline}, [h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="group of one hundred days"}[\${decNihPlus1Color()}]{.overline} will start once the residual \${decDohNidColor()}% of [h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="group of one hundred days"}[\${decNihAbsColor()}]{.overline} elapses from the current [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}: [\${TminusColor()}]{.overline}, and [h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="group of one hundred days"}[\${decNihAbsColor()}]{.overline} is \${decDohNidMidPadColor()}% finished from the current [nih](#nih){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer hectoday"} [mid](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"}: [\${decNihAbsColor()}]{.overline}\${decDohNidMidPadColor()}. The last digit of the [doh](#doh){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of hectoday"} is the [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} and the final digit of the 100−[doh](#doh){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of hectoday"} is (10 − [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"}) [mod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder) 10. ::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup07} $$\text{dox} = \text{doh} \href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder%20or%20signed%20remainder%20of%20a%20division}{\bmod} 10$$ {#eq-doh2dox} ::: Any kind of [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of year"} can be split into either an [x](#x){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="group of ten days"} and [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} or an [h](#h){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="group of one hundred days"} and [doh](#doh){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of hectoday"}, but the vinculum in a [mid](#mid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="mixed integer day of year"} can be used to emphasize one of these two options. If we want to categorize work and rest days based on [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of week"} as in the Gregorian calendar instead of [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} as in Decalendar, we can translate the "day of [era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calendar_era#:~:text=the%20period%20of%20time%20elapsed%20since%20one%20epoch%20of%20a%20calendar)" ([doe](#doe){#dayofera .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of era"}) equivalent of a year+day Dec date into a [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}. # Day of era (doe) {#sec-doe} Dec refers to midnight on [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[0]{.color0} as the [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}. At the [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}, the [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} [rolls over](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rollover#:~:text=the%20act%20of%20a%20counter%20restarting%20its%20count%20sequence) from [364]{.color364by365} or [365]{.color365by366} to [0]{.color0}. If the [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} did not reset to [-365]{.color0} or [-366]{.color0} at the [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}, it would continue from [-1]{.color364by365} to [0]{.color0} and thus become a [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"}. Therefore, the [doe](#doe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of era"} is like an [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"} that became a [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} at the "beginning of era" ([boe](#boe){#beginningofera .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of era"}) and never restarted before or after the [boe](#boe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of era"}, which is midnight on [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[0]{.color0} of Year [0]{.color0} (y[0]{.color0}). Each of the ten Dec time zones has its own [boe](#boe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of era"}, [doe](#doe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of era"}, [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}, and [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of year"}. The [boe](#boe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of era"} of the Zone [0]{.color0} Dec time zone is called the Dec [epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epoch#:~:text=an%20instant%20in%20time%20chosen%20as%20the%20origin%20of%20a%20particular%20calendar%20era). We can convert [Julian day numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_day#:~:text=a%20continuous%20count%20of%20days%20from%20the%20beginning%20of%20the%20Julian%20period) ([JDN](#jdn){#Juliandaynumber .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Julian day numbers"}) to Zone [0]{.color0} [doe](#doe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of era"} by subtracting the number of full days in between the start of the [Julian period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_day#Terminology:~:text=a%20chronological%20interval%20of%207980%C2%A0years) and the Dec epoch, which is 1721120 if the Zone [0]{.color0} time is later than noon and 1721119 otherwise. Dec uses [doe](#doe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of era"} for [calendrical calculations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calendrical_calculation#:~:text=a%20calculation%20concerning%20calendar%20dates), such as finding the [POSIX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/POSIX#:~:text=a%20family%20of%20standards%20specified%20by%20the%20IEEE%20Computer%20Society%20for%20maintaining%20compatibility%20between%20operating%20systems) [zero-based [dow]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/007904875/utilities/date.html#:~:text=weekday%20as%20a%20decimal%20number%20%5B0%2C6%5D%20(0%3Dsunday)) of a date. This year, the [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} of Christmas is \${xmasDotwColor()} according to @eq-dow: (\${xmasDote} + \${3 - nOffInput}) [mod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder) 7 = \${xmasDotwColor()}. Unlike [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of week"}, [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} can be found without much effort. The [dox](#dox){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of xún"} is the last digit of the [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} or equivalently the remainder after dividing the [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} by 10 as per @eq-dox: [299]{.color299by365} [mod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder) 10 = [9]{.color9}. ::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup08} $$\text{dow} = (\text{doe} + 3 - \href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iverson_bracket#:~:text=is%20defined%20to%20take%20the%20value%201%20for%20the%20values%20of%20the%20variables%20for%20which%20the%20statement%20is%20true%2C%20and%20takes%20the%20value%200%20otherwise}{[}\text{UTC offset} < 0\href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iverson_bracket#:~:text=is%20defined%20to%20take%20the%20value%201%20for%20the%20values%20of%20the%20variables%20for%20which%20the%20statement%20is%20true%2C%20and%20takes%20the%20value%200%20otherwise}{]}) \href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder%20or%20signed%20remainder%20of%20a%20division}{\bmod} 7$$ {#eq-dow} ::: @eq-dow is adapted from [Howard Hinnant](https://howardhinnant.github.io)'s [`weekday_from_days`](https://howardhinnant.github.io/date_algorithms.html#weekday_from_days) algorithm -@hinnant2021date. The Dec epoch [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} is [3]{.color3by7} = (0 + 3) [mod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder) 7. The [UNIX epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time#:~:text=00%3A00%3A00%20UTC%20on%201%C2%A0January%201970) [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} is [4]{.color4by7} = (719468 + 3) [mod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder) 7. Depending on how [mod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder) is [defined](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#Variants_of_the_definition), a negative [doe](#doe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of era"} could yield a negative [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}. We can add 7 to a negative [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} in the bottom row of @tbl-dow to obtain the positive [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} above it. ::: {#tbl-dow .overflowtable} | | Sun | Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Sat | | ---------- | -------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- | ---------------- | | [+]{.mono} | [0]{.color0} | [1]{.color1by7} | [2]{.color2by7} | [3]{.color3by7} | [4]{.color4by7} | [5]{.color5by7} | [6]{.color6by7} | | − | [7]{.color0} | [6]{.color1by7} | [5]{.color2by7} | [4]{.color3by7} | [3]{.color4by7} | [2]{.color5by7} | [1]{.color6by7} | ::: Christmas is an anchored⚓️holiday because it occurs on the same [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} every year. In contrast, floating🛟holidays like Thanksgiving are always planned for the same [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} and therefore can fall on various [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer days of year"}. We can use @eq-dowdif, which is derived from [Howard Hinnant](https://howardhinnant.github.io)'s [`weekday_difference`](https://howardhinnant.github.io/date_algorithms.html#weekday_difference) algorithm -@hinnant2021date, to find the floating holiday date in a given year. ::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup09} $$\text{dow}_\Delta = (\text{dow}_\text{M} - \text{dow}_\text{S} + 7) \href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder%20or%20signed%20remainder%20of%20a%20division}{\bmod} 7$$ {#eq-dowdif} ::: In @eq-dowdif, [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}~M~ is the [minuend](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/minuend#:~:text=A%20number%20or%20quantity%20from%20which%20another%20is%20to%20be%20subtracted), [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}~S~ is the [subtrahend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subtraction#:~:text=number%20being%20subtracted), and [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}~Δ~ is the [difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subtraction#Notation_and_terminology:~:text=The%20result%20is%20the%20difference) between them that ranges from [0]{.color0} to [6]{.color6by7}. To obtain the [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} of the first [Dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} [4]{.color4by7 .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Thursday"} after [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[266]{.color266by365}, which is Thanksgiving in the United States🇺🇸and Brazil🇧🇷, we plug [4]{.color4by7} as [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}~M~ and the [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} of [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[267]{.color267by365} as [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}~S~ into @eq-dowdif, \${day266dotwDiffColor()} = ([4]{.color4by7} − \${day266dotwColor} + 7) [mod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder) 7, and then add 267: \${day266dotwDiffPlus267Color} = \${day266dotwDiffColor()} + [267]{.color267by365}. ::: {.callout-warning} # Bad Pun Alert [**Deck**aday the halls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deck_the_Halls#:~:text=a%20traditional%20Christmas%20carol.) with [**dow~S~**]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of week"} of holly! Fa + la × 8! 'Tis the **[hectoday]{.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="hundred days"}** to be jolly! Aren't you thankful that I couldn't *thank* of a Thanksgiving pun? ::: When the current [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} is the minuend and [299]{.color299by365} is the subtrahend, the difference is the number of days *until* [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[299]{.color299by365} if it is negative or the days *since* [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[299]{.color299by365} if it is positive. The current difference tells us that \${xmasDiffColor()} \${xmasDiffDays} \${xmasDiffSince} [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[299]{.color299by365} of this year: \${decYearColor()}+[299]{.color299by365}[\${xmasDiffSign}]{.mono}\${xmasDiffColor()}. We can then subtract the [eoy](#eoy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="end of year"} to find the number of days until [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}[299]{.color299by365} of next year: \${nextYearColor()}+[299]{.color299by365}−\${xmasNextColor}. # Year of era (yoe) {#sec-yoe} To obtain a [doe](#doe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of era"} that we can plug into @eq-dow, we can use the two components of a Dec year+day date, namely a "year of era" ([yoe](#yoe){#yearofera .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="year of era"}) and a [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"}, to solve Equations -@eq-yoe2coe, -@eq-yoe2yoc, -@eq-date2doc, and -@eq-doe, which are based on [Howard Hinnant](https://howardhinnant.github.io)'s [`days_from_civil`](https://howardhinnant.github.io/date_algorithms.html#days_from_civil){.mono .under} algorithm that he describes in his manuscript entitled [[`chrono`]{.mono .under}-Compatible Low-Level Date Algorithms](https://howardhinnant.github.io/date_algorithms.html) -@hinnant2021date. ::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup10} $$\text{coe} = \biggl \lfloor \frac{\text{yoe}-399\ast\href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iverson_bracket#:~:text=is%20defined%20to%20take%20the%20value%201%20for%20the%20values%20of%20the%20variables%20for%20which%20the%20statement%20is%20true%2C%20and%20takes%20the%20value%200%20otherwise}{[}\text{yoe} \geq 0\href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iverson_bracket#:~:text=is%20defined%20to%20take%20the%20value%201%20for%20the%20values%20of%20the%20variables%20for%20which%20the%20statement%20is%20true%2C%20and%20takes%20the%20value%200%20otherwise}{]}}{400} \biggr \rfloor$$ {#eq-yoe2coe} $$\text{yoc} = \text{yoe} - \text{coe} \ast 400$$ {#eq-yoe2yoc} $$\text{doc} = \text{yoc} \ast 365 + \left\lfloor\frac{\text{yoc}}{4}\right\rfloor - \left\lfloor\frac{\text{yoc}}{100}\right\rfloor + \text{pid}$$ {#eq-date2doc} $$\text{doe} = \text{coe} \ast 146097 + \text{doc}$$ {#eq-doe} ::: :::{.panel-tabset group="language"} ### Julia ::: {.cell} ```{.julia .cell-code} function doe(year = 1969, pid = 306) coe = fld(year, 400) yoe = year - coe * 400 return coe * 146097 + yoe * 365 + fld(yoe, 4) - fld(yoe, 100) + pid end ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` doe (generic function with 3 methods) ``` ::: ```{.julia .cell-code} doe() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 719468 ``` ::: ::: ### Observable JavaScript ```{ojs} function doe(year = 1969, pid = 306) { const coe = Math.floor(year / 400), yoe = year - coe * 400; return coe * 146097 + yoe * 365 + Math.floor(yoe / 4) - Math.floor(yoe / 100) + pid } doe() ``` ### Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} def doe(year=1969, pid=306): coe = year // 400 yoe = year - coe * 400 return ( coe * 146097 + yoe * 365 + yoe // 4 - yoe // 100 + pid ) doe() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 719468 ``` ::: ::: ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} doe <- function(year = 1969, pid = 306) { coe <- year %/% 400 yoe <- year - coe * 400 coe * 146097 + yoe * 365 + yoe %/% 4 - yoe %/% 100 + pid } doe() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 719468 ``` ::: ::: ::: Equations -@eq-doe2coe, -@eq-doe2doc, -@eq-doe2yoc, -@eq-yoe, and -@eq-doe2pid below are based on [Howard Hinnant](https://howardhinnant.github.io)'s [`civil_from_days`](https://howardhinnant.github.io/date_algorithms.html#civil_from_days){.mono} algorithm and useful for obtaining Dec dates from [doe](#doe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of era"}, [UNIX timestamps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time#:~:text=the%20number%20of%20seconds%20that%20have%20elapsed%20since%2000%3A00%3A00%20UTC%20on%201%C2%A0January%201970), and [JDN](#jdn){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="Julian day numbers"} -@hinnant2021date. Regardless of whether we convert a [yoe](#yoe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="year of era"} and [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} to a [doe](#doe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of era"} or *vice versa*, along the way we calculate the "[cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_cycle_(calendar)#:~:text=the%20Gregorian%20cycle%20of%20400%20years%20has%20exactly%20146%2C097%20days%2C%20i.e.%20exactly%2020%2C871%20weeks%2C%20one%20can%20say%20that%20the%20Gregorian%20so%2Dcalled%20solar%20cycle%20lasts%20400%20years) of era" ([coe](#coe){#cycleofera .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="cycle of era"}), "year of cycle" ([yoc](#yoc){#yearofcycle .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="year of cycle"}), and "day of cycle" ([doc](#doc){#dayofcycle .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of cycle"}). ::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup11} $$\text{coe} = \left \lfloor \frac{\text{doe}-146096\ast\href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iverson_bracket#:~:text=is%20defined%20to%20take%20the%20value%201%20for%20the%20values%20of%20the%20variables%20for%20which%20the%20statement%20is%20true%2C%20and%20takes%20the%20value%200%20otherwise}{[}\text{doe} \geq 0\href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iverson_bracket#:~:text=is%20defined%20to%20take%20the%20value%201%20for%20the%20values%20of%20the%20variables%20for%20which%20the%20statement%20is%20true%2C%20and%20takes%20the%20value%200%20otherwise}{]}}{146097} \right \rfloor$$ {#eq-doe2coe} $$\text{doc} = \text{doe} - \text{coe} \ast 146097$$ {#eq-doe2doc} $$\text{yoc} = \Biggl \lfloor \frac{\text{doc} - \left\lfloor \dfrac{\text{doc}}{1460} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \dfrac{\text{doc}}{36524} \right\rfloor - \left\lfloor \dfrac{\text{doc}}{146096} \right\rfloor}{365} \Biggr \rfloor$$ {#eq-doe2yoc} $$\text{yoe} = \text{yoc} + \text{coe} \ast 400$$ {#eq-yoe} $$\text{pid} = \text{doc} - \text{yoc} \ast 365 - \left \lfloor \frac{\text{yoc}}{4} \right \rfloor + \left \lfloor \frac{\text{yoc}}{100} \right \rfloor$$ {#eq-doe2pid} ::: :::{.panel-tabset group="language"} ### Julia ::: {.cell} ```{.julia .cell-code} function date(doe = 719468) coe = fld(doe, 146097) doc = doe - coe * 146097 yoc = fld( doc - fld(doc, 1460) + fld(doc, 36524) - fld(doc, 146096), 365 ) return ( yoc + coe * 400, doc - ( yoc * 365 + fld(yoc, 4) - fld(yoc, 100) ) ) end ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` date (generic function with 2 methods) ``` ::: ```{.julia .cell-code} date() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` (1969, 306) ``` ::: ::: ### Observable JavaScript ```{ojs} function date(doe = 719468) { const coe = Math.floor(doe / 146097), doc = doe - coe * 146097, yoc = Math.floor( ( doc - Math.floor(doc / 1460) + Math.floor(doc / 36524) - Math.floor(doc / 146096) ) / 365 ); return [ yoc + coe * 400, doc - ( yoc * 365 + Math.floor(yoc / 4) - Math.floor(yoc / 100) ) ]; } date() ``` ### Python ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} def date(doe=719468): coe = doe // 146097 doc = doe - coe * 146097 yoc = ( doc - doc // 1460 + doc // 36524 - doc // 146096 ) // 365 return ( yoc + coe * 400, doc - ( yoc * 365 + yoc // 4 - yoc // 100 ) ) date() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` (1969, 306) ``` ::: ::: ### R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} date <- function(doe = 719468) { coe <- doe %/% 146097 doc <- doe - coe * 146097 yoc <- ( doc - doc %/% 1460 + doc %/% 36524 - doc %/% 146096 ) %/% 365 c( yoc + coe * 400, doc - ( yoc * 365 + yoc %/% 4 - yoc %/% 100 ) ) } date() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1969 306 ``` ::: ::: ::: Dates generated by Equations -@eq-doe2coe, -@eq-doe2doc, -@eq-doe2yoc, -@eq-yoe, and -@eq-doe2pid are guaranteed to be in the standard [yoe](#yoe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="year of era"}+[pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} format. Therefore, we can standardize Dec dates by converting them to [doe](#doe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of era"} and then back to dates again. A [round-trip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-trip_format_conversion#:~:text=converting%20from%20any%20data%20representation%20and%20back%20again) "date to [doe](#doe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of era"} to date" conversion ensures that the [yoe](#yoe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="year of era"} is an integer and the [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} is a non-negative integer less than the [eoy](#eoy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="end of year"}: [0]{.color0} ≤ [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} < [eoy](#eoy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="end of year"}. # Day of week (dow) {#sec-dow} Even though Decalendar functions best with [x](#x){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="groups of ten days"}, Dec dates can display [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of week"} by expanding a [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} into a "beginning of week" ([bow](#bow){#beginningofweek .tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"}) and a POSIX zero-based [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}. To calculate the [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"}, we subtract the [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} from the [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"}: [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"} = [pid](#pid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="positive integer day of year"} − [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}. According to the current Zone [0]{.color0} [[yoe](#yoe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="year of era"}+[bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"}+[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}]{.nowrap} date, [\${decYearColor()}[\${dotw0sign}]{.mono}\${dotw0dotyPadColor()}+\${dotwColor()}]{.nowrap}, the most recent [Dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of week"} [0]{.color0} was on [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}\${dotw0dotyColor()} and today is [Dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of week"} \${dotwColor()}. ::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup12} $$\text{yoe} + \frac{\text{pid}}{\text{eoy}} = \text{yoe} + \frac{\text{bow + dow}}{\text{eoy}}$$ {#eq-bow} ::: A Dec [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"} date can have a countup or a countdown [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"}. The countdown equivalent of [\${decYearColor()}[\${dotw0sign}]{.mono}\${dotw0dotyPadColor()}+\${dotwColor()}]{.nowrap} is [\${nextYearColor()}−\${dotw0dotyNegColor}+\${dotwColor()}]{.nowrap}. Like [nid](#nid){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="negative integer day of year"}, countdown [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"} can be useful. We can add up to 52 weeks to any countdown [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"} without having to take into account the length of the year. The sum of 52 weeks and the last [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"}+[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of week"} of this year is 52 × 7 + \${decYearLastBowNegColor} + \${decYearLastDowColor()} = \${decYearLastBowSumColor} + \${decYearLastDowColor()}. Based on the calculation above, the Dec [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"} date which is 52 weeks after [\${nextYearColor()}−\${decYearLastBowNegColor1}[+]{.mono}\${decYearLastDowColor()}]{.nowrap} is [\${nextYearColor()}[+]{.mono}\${decYearLastBowSumColor1}[+]{.mono}\${decYearLastDowColor()}]{.nowrap}. When we see the same [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of week"} in two dates, we know that their difference is a multiple of 7. The [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"} can be used to identify a [woy](#woy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="week of year"} in phrases like "the week of [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}\${dotw0dotyPadColor()}" or "the week that begins on [d](#d){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day"}\${dotw0dotyPadColor()}". Years with the same [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} also have matching [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginnings of week"}. The [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} is the [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} of the first day of the Dec year. To obtain the current [woy](#woy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="week of year"}, we sum the [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} with the [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"} then divide by 7 as in @eq-woy: \${woyColor()} = (\${doty0dotwColor} + \${dotw0dotyPadColor()}) ÷ 7. Like the [eoy](#eoy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="end of year"}, the [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} is omitted from Dec dates, because we can specify dates without it and derive it from the [yoe](#yoe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="year of era"}. The result of turning a [yoe](#yoe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="year of era"} first into a [doe](#doe){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of era"} and then into a [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} is a [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}. ::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup13} $$\text{woy} = \dfrac{\text{bow}+\text{boydow}}{7}$$ {#eq-woy} ::: We can also convert a [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"} into a [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} using @eq-boydow. If [dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of week"} were like [doy](#doy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="days of year"} and reset at every [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}, we would not need the [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} because it would always be zero and conversion between [woy](#woy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="week of year"} and [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"} dates would be straightforward, but the reality is that the [boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"} can be any integer from zero to six and is required to convert between [woy](#woy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="week of year"} and [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"} dates. ::: {.equationgroup #equationgroup14} $$\text{boydow} = (7 - \text{bow}\href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder%20or%20signed%20remainder%20of%20a%20division}{\bmod}7)\href{https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo#:~:text=returns%20the%20remainder%20or%20signed%20remainder%20of%20a%20division}{\bmod}7$$ {#eq-boydow} ::: By rearranging @eq-woy, we can see that [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginnings of week"} should expand to [7×[woy](#woy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="week of year"}−[boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}]{.nowrap}, but [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginnings of week"} and [woy](#woy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="weeks of year"} are interchangeable in Dec dates as if they were equivalent: [bow](#bow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of week"} = [~~7×~~[woy](#woy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="week of year"}~~−[boy](#boy){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="beginning of year"}[dow](#dow){.tool data-bs-toggle="tooltip" data-bs-title="day of week"}~~]{.nowrap}.
